title: Arsenal face tense match against Sunderland, raising alarms
seoTitle: Arsenal face tense Sunderland clash as alarms ring
subtitle: Balanced match sparks concern over Ben White injury and attacking frustration
excerpt: Arsenal struggle against Sunderland in a match marked by concern over a Ben White injury and wasted chances in attack.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Arsenal face a challenging scenario in their match against Sunderland, who are going toe-to-toe with the reigning champions. The London side, known as the Gunners, are experiencing moments of frustration in a balanced clash at the Stadium of Light. The flow of the game and the physical condition of their players explain why the club has become one of the most searched topics.

Concern over Ben White injury

During the match, Arsenal defender Ben White sparked serious concern after picking up what appeared to be a groin injury. The physical issue occurred in the moments leading up to halftime. Despite the pain and apparent discomfort, the player remained on the pitch to help his team before the end of the first half, leaving doubts about whether he will continue for the second half.

Attacking frustration and wasted chances

The Gunners' attack struggled to break down the opponent's defense, leading to feelings of frustration. In one of the most dangerous plays of the first half, Bukayo Saka cushioned a header toward Kai Havertz. However, Granit Xhaka managed to clear the ball with his boot before the German could finish the play. In addition, Calafiori has been causing problems for the opposition with his attacking runs.

Opponent pressure and refereeing performance

Sunderland have shown great diligence in their defensive pressing and plenty of energy with and without the ball, keeping a clean sheet for over half an hour. Nilson Angulo went down inside the penalty area, but the officiating crew waved away the penalty appeals from the home fans. Referee John Brooks has adopted a highly permissive approach, letting play continue despite shirt-pulling and grappling occurring during almost every corner kick.

Analysis and commentary on tactical performance

Manager Arteta's stance and decisions also came under scrutiny during the matchday. Comments shared on broadcast channels suggest that the manager could be considered foolish at times, even from the perspective of the club's own fans. Former Leeds forward Lucy Ward, commentating for TNT Sports, pointed out that the longer Sunderland stay in the game, the more the atmosphere and the players' belief are likely to grow.

With information from BBC, The Guardian.
